summary: Extends IKEv2 so peers can periodically repeat mutual authentication, which matters in remote-access setups. This limits how long a third party who has taken control of a peer can keep using security associations. It is experimental.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4478 adds a way for an IKEv2 responder to tell its peer when to authenticate again. The initiator should repeat the Initial exchange before that time expires, or the responder may close the security associations.

subtitle: A responder can set a deadline for repeating mutual authentication.

tldr.problem: In some remote-access settings, policy requires peers to repeat mutual authentication, but a gateway may not be able to start an exchange that needs user credentials.
tldr.mechanism: The responder sends an AUTH_LIFETIME notification with the time remaining before the initiator should repeat the Initial exchange.
tldr.outcome: The Experimental extension lets a responder request repeated authentication. Rekeying an IKE security association is a separate operation.

today: RFC 4478 defines an Experimental extension to IKEv2. The unit metadata lists no later RFC that updates or replaces it.

sections.title: Why Repeat Authentication
sections.content:
Some policies require IKEv2 peers to repeat mutual authentication periodically. In remote access, a human may need to provide credentials, often through the Extensible Authentication Protocol (EAP), so the gateway may not be able to initiate the exchange itself.

RFC 4478 lets the original responder tell the original initiator how many seconds remain before authentication must be repeated. The RFC distinguishes this from rekeying an IKE security association.
sections.plainLanguage: The gateway can set a time for the user side to authenticate again. This is separate from replacing the keys in an existing security association.

sections.title: The AUTH_LIFETIME Notification
sections.content:
The responder sends an AUTH_LIFETIME notification either in the final message of the IKE_AUTH exchange or in an INFORMATIONAL request. The notification gives the number of seconds before the initiator should repeat the Initial exchange; time is measured from when the initiator receives it.

The initiator SHOULD repeat the exchange before the lifetime ends. A lifetime of zero means to begin immediately. The RFC says values below 300 seconds or above 86400 seconds are usually unreasonable. If the initiator does not re-authenticate, the responder may delete the security associations.
sections.plainLanguage: The notification gives the initiator a time limit, in seconds. The initiator should authenticate again before the limit expires; zero means to start right away.

sections.title: Peers Without Support
sections.content:
An IKEv2 implementation that does not support AUTH_LIFETIME ignores the notification and does not repeat authentication because of it. In that case, the original responder sends a Delete notification for the IKE security association.

A responder that does not support this extension simply does not send the notification. An initiator may also require more frequent authentication than the notification requests; the notification does not override its policy.
sections.plainLanguage: An older peer may ignore the request. The responder can then delete the security association, while the initiator can still require authentication sooner.

sections.title: Security Policy and IANA
sections.content:
The RFC says the responder's notification does not override the initiator's security policy. An initiator may set reasonable limits on the lifetime it accepts, including rejecting a very short value.

IANA assigned a notification payload type for AUTH_LIFETIME in the IKEv2 Notify Message Types registry.
sections.plainLanguage: The initiator remains free to require stricter re-authentication than the responder asks for. IANA assigned a notification type for this message.
